summary: Ontario tower-layer point with a verified location, no build date, height or manufacturer recorded, and no readable source on its history or site today.

sources.title: Tower layer record, LIO_Open10 layer 14 (Fire Tower subtype)
sources.publisher: Land Information Ontario, Government of Ontario

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

evidence.supports: Named Trout Lake Fire Tower in the Ontario tower layer
Classed as a fire tower point
Point coordinates as stated in the story
Location came from an AFFM tower dataset
evidence.quote: "GENERAL_COMMENTS":"Location provided by AFFM Tower dataset - TOWER"

evidence.supports: No height, manufacturer or construction date recorded
Most towers erected 1920s to 1950s, when forest fire protection was at its height
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Aerial spotting took over in the 1960s and towers were used less
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: A decision to destroy many towers, made to avoid lawsuits from climbers
evidence.quote: The government decided that they didn't want any lawsuits on their hands in case careless citizens climbed the unmanned towers and were injured in the process.

evidence.supports: A decision was made to have many destroyed
evidence.quote: The decision then went through to have many destroyed.

evidence.supports: Destruction done with explosives or by crews taking towers apart
evidence.quote: This was done by either placing TNT charges at the base footings to blow them down, or by forest ranger crews who took them apart piece by piece.

evidence.supports: The record gives no location description for the site

notes_for_editor: Same evidence base: the LIO tower-layer record for 'Trout Lake Fire Tower' (coordinates, location accuracy, verified flag, AFFM note, null height and construction fields), plus the forestrangers general history. The name is not tied in any source to a particular lake, so the story does not name one. Do not confuse this record with the layer's 'Big Trout Fire Tower' (Fontaine Twp), about 21 km north, which the cached still-standing list calls the Fontaine Tower at Big Trout Lake. Searches and firelookout.ca slug found nothing on this tower. Not established: build year, height, staffing, fate, status, access, site today. The brief gives no local_unit, so the story says Ontario only. Confidence is low because the layer is the only record.
